name: South Corner
approach: From the Staircase Ranger Station (~770-850 ft, at the end of Lake Cushman Rd/North Fork Skokomish Rd), the approach starts on the North Fork Skokomish River Trail, a gently graded old decommissioned roadbed that runs up-valley through old-growth forest for about 3.7-3.8 miles to the former road-end/Spike Camp junction with the Flapjack Lakes Trail. Bear onto the Flapjack Lakes Trail, which climbs steadily and then steeply (with one rough slide/washout bypass to pick through) for roughly 3.4-4.1 more miles, gaining about 2,000 ft, to reach Flapjack Lakes (~3,850 ft, about 7.5-8 miles from the trailhead) - the standard base camp. Flapjack Lakes is a designated, permit-limited backcountry camp, so reserve ahead for summer weekends. Reliable water is available at the lakes and at several creek crossings on the lower trail; treat before drinking. From camp, continue about 1.5 miles on maintained trail up-basin toward Gladys Divide; just before the divide, leave the trail and climb southeast up a steep snow/scree couloir (several hundred feet of gain, often 35-40+ degrees) to Needle Pass. This couloir holds firm, icy snow well into summer, and crampons plus an ice axe are advisable for most of the season - it's the single biggest hazard of the approach, since a slip on hard snow here has real consequences. From Needle Pass, turn left (east) and scramble exposed Class 3 terrain to the summit of Beta Peak, descend through its right-most summit notch (one Class 4 move and a short gully), traverse high toward Cruiser, then drop down a longer connecting gully to reach Cruiser's base, where the roped climbing begins (a Class 4 gully leads to a large chockstone; go left around it and squeeze through a short tunnel to reach the platform below the 5.0 pitch). All told this is roughly 8-9 miles from the trailhead to the base of the technical climbing, crossing Needle Pass at about 5,700 ft on the way, typically 5-7 hours to camp and another push to the base the next day. Fog and low cloud are common on the ridge and ridge-basin route-finding above Flapjack Lakes is easy to lose in flat light, so know the boot-tread line before committing.
